steps.title: A stream whose answer is known
steps.text: Opening the plugin already started a simulated stream and the Acquisition fit window: watch its Decay page fill, then Correlation, MCS and Macro time. The stream has two species with donor lifetimes 3.4 ns and 1.1 ns.

steps.title: Load the example again
steps.text: Load example simulates (or reuses) the demo stream, registers it as a dataset and opens a new Acquisition fit window for it.

steps.title: Select source
steps.text: Choose Simulation, Becker-Hickl, PicoQuant, or BrickMic. Selecting hardware does not scan or contact it.

await.hint: Choose the source you intend to use.

steps.title: Initialize explicitly
steps.text: Press Initialize device before Start. A missing driver or unavailable card is reported here rather than silently falling back to simulation.

steps.title: Bound the run
steps.text: Keep at least one positive stop condition. Time is wall-clock; photon count is decoded by the live pipeline.

await.hint: Set a time and/or photon limit.

steps.title: Map routing channels
steps.text: These four controls are the pipeline decay-window routing order. Match them to your instrument's channels before starting.

steps.title: Define the simulated sample
steps.text: Simulation setup opens the species table (molecules, diffusion, per-colour brightness, background, decay), the kinetics rate grids and the geometry. OK validates it with the simulator engine and uses it for the next run. Advanced simulation parameters shows the same dictionary as raw JSON.

await.hint: Press Simulation setup… and review the species table.

steps.title: Start and stop
steps.text: Start streams FIFO or encoded simulator records through AcquisitionPipeline. Stop interrupts the active source and flushes its result state.

await.hint: Press Start when the source is initialized.

steps.title: Inspect results
steps.text: The plots fill while the run is going: decay, correlation, count rate, MCS and macrotime, each tab with its own controls (channel pairs, binning, Set to mean, bin width, update rate). Clear removes displayed state; Reset does not contact a device.
